alerts.title: Alert rules
alerts.intro: What becomes an emergency, what is only a signal, and how long to wait. These are the organization’s rules; any product can change its own.

levelHint.signal: Out of normal. No message: highlighted in its area and in the daily summary.

monitor_down.title: Site or API down
monitor_down.body: A site or /health monitor failed 3 checks in a row. If it comes back before the wait, nobody is told.
monitor_down.info: Octadash checks every minute. One failure can be the network; three in a row is the site. Then it waits the minutes you set and, if it is still down, tells the channels and opens the red strip. Use 0 for checkout or login, where every minute counts.

heartbeat_missed.title: Heartbeat missed
heartbeat_missed.body: A cron job, backup or worker did not check in within its interval plus grace.
heartbeat_missed.info: Each heartbeat has its own interval and grace. When both pass without a check-in, the job is late and this rule decides what happens.
heartbeat_missed.note: Grace is set on each heartbeat.

cert_expiring.title: Certificate expiring
cert_expiring.body: The HTTPS certificate of a monitor expires soon.
cert_expiring.info: Octadash reads the certificate on every check. Most certificates renew on their own about 30 days before they expire; if one is still old this close, the renewal failed.

error_spike.title: Error spike
error_spike.body: A product’s errors in the last 15 minutes reach a multiple of its normal for this time of day, with a minimum so a quiet product does not fire on 3 errors.
error_spike.info: Normal is the same hour on each of the last 7 days. Errors of ignored issues never count. It closes on its own when the last 15 minutes fall back under the rule. A product with no history fires on the minimum alone.

key_event_stopped.title: Key event stopped
key_event_stopped.body: An event you marked as key (a sign-up, a payment) stops arriving at an hour it usually comes.
key_event_stopped.info: Octadash waits for the time the expected number of events normally takes at this hour (the same hour of the last 7 days), and never less than the minimum silence. Quiet hours wait longer on their own, and an event too rare at this hour (under 5 a day) never fires. It closes when the next event arrives. Mark key events in Set up Product usage.

log_alert.title: Log alert
log_alert.body: A saved Logs search with Alert on matches a line. Each product with a match gets its own emergency.
log_alert.info: Turn Alert on for a saved search on the Logs page. Octadash runs it every minute over the lines since it was turned on. It closes after the minutes you set pass without a match (at most 60). Only lines that arrive after Alert is on can fire it.

payments_failing.title: Payments failing
payments_failing.body: Failed charges at the gateway well above normal. Each product gets its own emergency.
payments_failing.info: Octadash reads the charges of the last 15 minutes every minute. It opens when the share that failed reaches the percent you set, with at least the number of charges you set, so two failures at night do not wake anyone. It closes when the share falls back under.

cost_runaway.title: Cost runaway
cost_runaway.body: Spend in one hour well above a normal hour (AI tokens today; cloud when it arrives). Each product gets its own emergency.
cost_runaway.info: Octadash compares each product’s latest hour of spend with its average hour over the last 7 days. It opens when the hour reaches the times you set and at least the dollars you set, so a few cents never wake anyone. Shared accounts count only the product’s part. It closes when an hour falls back under, or after 6 hours without spend.

new_issue.title: New issue
new_issue.body: A message each time an error is seen for the first time. Off by default: the Error spike already tells when errors climb, and a busy product makes new issues every day.
new_issue.info: It sends only a message: it never opens an emergency or turns the strip red. New issues in the same minute go out as one message per channel. An issue that comes back after being resolved shows under Regressed in Errors.
new_issue.note: Several new issues in the same minute come as one message.

why.body: A backup that stops running fails in silence: nothing is down, nothing errors, and you find out the day you need it. A heartbeat turns silence into an emergency.
why.good: Good for backups, cron jobs, queue workers, certificate renewals and nightly imports.

features.title: Grouped, not repeated

features.title: Alert in your channel

features.title: Private by default
features.body: The IP address is never stored. An e-mail becomes a hash. Errors are kept 90 days.
